overview: Two gel electrophoresis approaches for separating proteins, distinguished by whether the protein's native structure and charge are preserved.
genZNote: SDS-PAGE strips proteins down to their skeleton. Native PAGE lets them keep their outfit.

aspects.label: Principle
aspects.valueA: Denatures proteins with SDS (uniform negative charge) and separates them purely by molecular weight.
aspects.valueB: Separates proteins in their native folded state, based on a combination of size, shape, and intrinsic charge.

aspects.label: Target
aspects.valueB: Intact, natively folded proteins or protein complexes.

aspects.label: Key Reagents
aspects.valueA: SDS (sodium dodecyl sulfate), often with a reducing agent (e.g. DTT or beta-mercaptoethanol) to break disulfide bonds.
aspects.valueB: No SDS or reducing agent — buffers preserve native pH, ionic strength, and folding.

aspects.label: What It Reveals
aspects.valueA: Approximate molecular weight and subunit composition.
aspects.valueB: Native size, oligomeric state, and sometimes retained enzymatic activity (via in-gel activity assays).

aspects.label: Separation Basis
aspects.valueA: Molecular weight only, since charge-to-mass ratio is normalized by SDS.
aspects.valueB: Charge, shape, and size combined — migration does not correlate simply with molecular weight.

aspects.label: Limitations / Pitfalls
aspects.valueA: Destroys native structure and any activity/binding information.
aspects.valueB: Harder to interpret band size; some proteins may not enter the gel well or may aggregate.

aspects.label: Applications
aspects.valueA: Western blotting, estimating protein size and purity.
aspects.valueB: Preserving enzyme activity for in-gel assays, studying protein-protein interactions and complexes.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Non-denaturing; separates by native charge, shape, and size.
